questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a defining feature of all living organisms, without any exception?

solution.explanation: Growth and increase in mass are also shown by non-living things (a mountain or sand mound grows by accumulation of material on its surface), and many living organisms do not reproduce. Metabolism, the sum of all chemical reactions in the body, is found in every living organism and in no non-living object.
steps: Growth / increase in mass: also seen in non-living objects → not defining
Reproduction: absent in mules, sterile worker bees → not defining
Metabolism: present in all living organisms, absent in non-living things → defining
solution.why_others_wrong: Growth and increase in body mass occur in non-living objects too (by accumulation on the surface); reproduction is absent in several living organisms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', What is 'living'?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Metabolism

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The families Felidae and Canidae are placed together in the order:

solution.explanation: An order is a group of related families. Felidae (cats) and Canidae (dogs) share several features and are grouped in the animal order Carnivora.
steps: Family Felidae (e.g. Panthera, Felis) and family Canidae → order Carnivora
solution.why_others_wrong: Primata is the order of monkeys, gorilla and gibbon (and man). Polymoniales and Sapindales are plant orders.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic categories (order)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Carnivora

solution.explanation: Names of plants follow the agreed principles of the ICBN; animal names follow the ICZN. Classification systems group organisms but do not lay down naming rules.
solution.why_others_wrong: ICZN is for animals. The two- and five-kingdom systems are systems of classification, not codes of naming.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option C: International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A viroid differs from a virus in that a viroid:

options.text: is a free DNA enclosed in a protein coat
is a protein that lacks nucleic acid
is a free RNA that lacks a protein coat

solution.explanation: T.O. Diener (1971) found that the agent of potato spindle tuber disease is a free RNA of low molecular weight. It lacks the protein coat found in viruses, hence the name viroid.
steps: Viroid = free, low molecular weight RNA
solution.why_others_wrong: No virus or viroid has both DNA and RNA. A viroid's nucleic acid is RNA, not DNA. A protein without nucleic acid describes a prion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option D: is a free RNA that lacks a protein coat

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about members of kingdom Protista are correct?

(a) The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica, which makes them indestructible.
(b) Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax can multiply so rapidly that the sea appears red.
(c) Euglenoids have a cellulose cell wall.
(d) The spores of slime moulds possess true walls and are extremely resistant.
(e) Most dinoflagellates live in fresh water.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Kingdom Protista: chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds
solution.explanation: Diatom walls form two thin overlapping shells embedded with silica. Red tides are caused by rapid multiplication of red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax. Euglenoids have no cell wall; instead they have a protein-rich pellicle. Slime mould spores have true walls and survive for many years. Dinoflagellates are mostly marine.
steps: (a) True: silica walls, accumulate as diatomaceous earth
(c) False: euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle, not a cell wall
(d) True: resistant spores dispersed by air
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement (c) is the usual trap: the flexible pellicle of Euglena is not a cell wall.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (class of fungi) with List-II (example).

List-I:
A. Phycomycetes
B. Ascomycetes
C. Basidiomycetes
D. Deuteromycetes

List-II:
I. Agaricus
II. Mucor
III. Alternaria
IV. Neurospora

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium (Mucor, Rhizopus, Albugo). Ascomycetes are sac fungi (Neurospora, Aspergillus, Claviceps). Basidiomycetes include mushrooms (Agaricus), smuts and rusts. Deuteromycetes are the imperfect fungi (Alternaria, Colletotrichum, Trichoderma).
solution.why_others_wrong: Neurospora is a sac fungus (ascomycete), not a mushroom; Alternaria has no known sexual stage, so it is a deuteromycete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Members of Deuteromycetes are commonly called imperfect fungi.
Reason (R): Only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A fungus is called 'imperfect' because its sexual stage is not known; only its asexual or vegetative phase has been seen. When the sexual stage of such a fungus is discovered, it is moved to the class it belongs to. So R is exactly why they are called imperfect.
steps: R: only asexual/vegetative phases known → true
The missing sexual stage is the reason for the name → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Deuteromycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a lichen, the algal partner is called the mycobiont.
Statement II: Lichens do not grow in polluted areas, so they are good indicators of pollution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A lichen is a mutually useful association of an alga and a fungus. The algal component is the phycobiont and the fungal component is the mycobiont. The alga makes food; the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas.
steps: Algal partner = phycobiont, fungal partner = mycobiont → Statement I false
Lichens are absent from polluted areas → Statement II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens (lichens)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about taxonomic categories are correct?

(a) Lion, tiger and leopard are species of the same genus.
(b) The families Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in the same order, mainly on the basis of floral characters.
(c) In plants, classes with a few similar characters are grouped into a higher category called division.
(d) As we go up from species to kingdom, the number of characters common to the members of a category increases.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Lion (Panthera leo), leopard (P. pardus) and tiger (P. tigris) belong to the genus Panthera. Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are placed in the order Polymoniales mainly on floral characters. In plants, the category above class is called division (phylum in animals). Higher categories hold more kinds of organisms, which share fewer characters.
steps: (b) True: order Polymoniales, based on floral characters
(c) True: division is used for plants
(d) False: common characters decrease going up
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement (d) reverses the rule: the higher the category, the broader it is and the fewer characters its members share.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic categories
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reproduction cannot be taken as an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.
Reason (R): Many organisms, such as mules, sterile worker bees and infertile human couples, do not reproduce.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

solution.concept: Why reproduction is not a defining feature of life
solution.explanation: A defining feature must be present in every living organism. NCERT points out that mules, sterile worker bees and infertile human couples are living but do not reproduce, so reproduction cannot define life. R states exactly these exceptions, so it explains A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (kingdom) with List-II (cell wall).

List-I:
A. Monera
B. Fungi
C. Plantae
D. Animalia

List-II:
I. Absent
II. Present, made of cellulose
III. Non-cellulosic, made of polysaccharide and amino acids
IV. Present, without cellulose (chitin and polysaccharides)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Characteristics of the five kingdoms (cell wall)
solution.explanation: Bacteria have a non-cellulosic wall of polysaccharide and amino acids. Fungal walls lack cellulose and are made of chitin and polysaccharides. Plant cell walls are mainly cellulose. Animal cells have no cell wall.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Table: characteristics of the five kingdoms; Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Read the following statements about the features of living organisms.

(a) Metabolic reactions demonstrated in a test tube (in vitro) are living things.
(b) Photoperiod affects reproduction in seasonal breeders, both plants and animals.
(c) Human beings are the only organisms that are aware of themselves (self-conscious).
(d) In animals, growth by cell division continues throughout the life span.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things, though they are living reactions. All organisms sense their environment; photoperiod, for example, affects reproduction in seasonal breeders. Only humans have self-consciousness. Plants grow by cell division throughout life, but animals grow only up to a certain age (cell division continues only to replace lost cells).
steps: (a) False: in vitro reactions are not living things
(c) True: self-consciousness is unique to humans
(d) False: true of plants, not animals
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) describes plants. In animals, growth stops at a certain age.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', What is 'living'?
solution.final_answer: Option B: (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are rules of binomial nomenclature?

(a) Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics.
(b) The first word of the name is the genus and the second is the specific epithet.
(c) Both words of the name begin with a capital letter.
(d) When handwritten, the two words are underlined separately.
(e) The author's name, in abbreviated form, is written after the specific epithet.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each name has a generic name and a specific epithet, Latinised and printed in italics (underlined separately when handwritten). The genus begins with a capital letter, the specific epithet with a small letter. The author's name comes at the end in abbreviated form, e.g. Mangifera indica Linn.
steps: (c) False: the specific epithet starts with a small letter
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (c) is wrong: 'Mangifera Indica' is incorrectly written.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Nomenclature (binomial nomenclature)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Viruses have an inert crystalline structure outside a living cell.
(b) Some viruses contain both DNA and RNA.
(c) Viruses that infect plants generally have single-stranded RNA.
(d) Bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.
(e) Prions are infectious agents made of abnormally folded RNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Viruses are non-cellular and inert outside a host cell. Their genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both. Plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA; animal viruses have single- or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA; bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA. Prions are abnormally folded proteins.
steps: (b) False: no virus contains both RNA and DNA
(e) False: prions consist of abnormally folded protein
solution.why_others_wrong: (b) and (e) are false, so only the combination (a), (c), (d) fits.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Bryophytes are called the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' because they:

options.text: live partly in fresh water and partly in sea water
live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction
have both aquatic roots and aerial leaves
have a free-living sporophyte and a free-living gametophyte

solution.explanation: Bryophytes grow on land, usually in damp, shaded places, but their male gametes (antherozoids) need water to swim to the archegonium.
steps: Fertilisation: antherozoids reach the egg through water

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about bryophytes are correct?

(a) The main plant body is haploid and produces gametes.
(b) The sporophyte is free-living and independent of the gametophyte.
(c) The antherozoids are biflagellate.
(d) Some cells of the sporophyte undergo meiosis to form haploid spores.
(e) Each archegonium produces many eggs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The dominant bryophyte plant is the haploid gametophyte. The antheridium makes biflagellate antherozoids; the flask-shaped archegonium makes a single egg. steps: (b) False: sporophyte is attached to and nourished by the gametophyte
(e) False: archegonium has a single egg
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes

solution.why_others_wrong: Equisetum (horsetail) is the sphenopsid; Adiantum is a fern (Pteropsida).

solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reproduction and structure in algae are correct?

(a) Spirogyra shows fusion of non-flagellated gametes that are similar in size.
(b) Volvox and Fucus show fusion of a large, non-motile female gamete with a smaller, motile male gamete.
(c) Some species of Eudorina show fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size.
(d) Members of Phaeophyceae have two equal, apical flagella.
(e) Members of Chlorophyceae store food as mannitol and laminarin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Sexual reproduction and features of algae
solution.explanation: Isogamy with non-flagellated gametes: Spirogyra. Anisogamy: some species of Eudorina. Oogamy (large static egg, small motile male gamete): Volvox, Fucus. Brown algae have two unequal, laterally attached flagella. Green algae store starch; mannitol and laminarin are the reserves of brown algae.
steps: (d) False: brown algae have 2 unequal lateral flagella
(e) False: mannitol and laminarin are brown-algal reserves
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) swap features between classes: 2–8 equal apical flagella and starch belong to green algae; unequal lateral flagella and laminarin to brown algae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (reproduction; table of algal classes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Heterosporous pteridophytes such as Selaginella and Salvinia show an event considered a precursor to the seed habit.
Reason (R): In them, the female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte for a variable period, and the zygote develops into a young embryo within the female gametophyte.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In heterosporous pteridophytes, megaspores and microspores give rise to female and male gametophytes. The female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte, and the zygote develops into an embryo within it. NCERT calls this event a precursor to the seed habit. R describes that event, so it explains A.
steps: The retention of the female gametophyte and development of the embryo within it is the event called the precursor of the seed habit → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes (heterospory)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about liverworts and mosses are correct?

(a) The gametophyte of a moss has two stages: the protonema and the leafy stage.
(b) Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds formed in gemma cups on liverwort thalli.
(c) Mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal.
(d) The leafy stage of mosses bears true leaves with vascular tissue.
(e) The sporophyte of mosses is more elaborate than that of liverworts.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Moss gametophyte: a creeping, green, branched filamentous protonema and an upright leafy stage. Liverworts like Marchantia reproduce asexually by gemmae from gemma cups. Bryophytes lack true roots, stem and leaves and have no vascular tissue. The moss sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) is more elaborate than the liverwort sporophyte, and mosses have an elaborate spore-dispersal mechanism.
steps: (d) False: bryophytes lack true leaves and vascular tissue
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (liverworts, mosses)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, pollen grains are carried to the ovules by water currents.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Gymnosperm gametophytes remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophyte. Pollen grains are released from microsporangia and carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules; the pollen tube carries the male gametes to the archegonia. Water is not needed.
steps: Statement II: false, pollen is carried by air currents
solution.why_others_wrong: Dependence on water for fertilisation is a feature of bryophytes and pteridophytes, not gymnosperms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. These roots help the plant to:

solution.explanation: Swampy soil is poor in oxygen. The upward-growing roots of Rhizophora, called pneumatophores, help the plant get oxygen for respiration.
steps: Pneumatophores grow above ground → obtain oxygen for respiration
solution.why_others_wrong: Food storage is seen in carrot, turnip and sweet potato roots; support is given by prop and stilt roots.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root (modifications of root)
solution.final_answer: Option C: get oxygen for respiration

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The tendrils of cucumber and pumpkin develop from:

solution.explanation: Stem tendrils develop from axillary buds. They are slender, spirally coiled and help gourds (cucumber, pumpkin, watermelon) and grapevines to climb.
steps: Tendril position: in the axil of a leaf → axillary bud → stem tendril
solution.why_others_wrong: In pea, tendrils are modified leaves (leaflets), not stems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Stem (modifications of stem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: axillary buds

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Twisted aestivation, in which one margin of each petal overlaps the next one, is found in:

solution.explanation: In twisted aestivation one margin of each appendage overlaps the next one in a regular way, as in china rose, lady's finger and cotton.
solution.why_others_wrong: Calotropis has valvate aestivation (margins only touch), Cassia imbricate and pea vexillary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (aestivation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: China rose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a mango fruit, the edible part is the:

solution.explanation: Mango is a drupe. Its pericarp has a thin epicarp, a fleshy edible mesocarp and a stony hard endocarp.
solution.why_others_wrong: A fibrous mesocarp is found in coconut, not mango.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Fruit
solution.final_answer: Option B: fleshy mesocarp

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Solanaceae is commonly called the 'potato family'.
Statement II: Liliaceae is a family of dicotyledonous plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Solanaceae is the potato family. Liliaceae, the lily family, is a characteristic representative of monocotyledonous plants.
steps: Statement II: false, Liliaceae is a monocot family
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of some important families
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (modification).

List-I:
A. Banyan
B. Maize
C. Pistia
D. Opuntia

List-II:
I. Flattened green stem that carries out photosynthesis
II. Supporting roots arising from the lower nodes of the stem
III. Hanging roots from branches that support the tree
IV. Lateral branch with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Banyan has prop roots hanging from its branches. Maize and sugarcane have stilt roots from the lower nodes. Aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia have lateral branches with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots. Opuntia has a flattened green photosynthetic stem.
solution.why_others_wrong: Prop roots (banyan) hang from branches; stilt roots (maize) arise from the lowest nodes. Mixing the two is the usual error.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root; The Stem (modifications)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a racemose inflorescence, the flowers are borne in basipetal succession.
Reason (R): In a racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In a racemose inflorescence the main axis keeps growing, so new flowers keep forming at the top: the flowers are borne laterally in acropetal succession (older below, younger above). Basipetal order is seen in cymose inflorescence, where the main axis ends in a flower.
steps: R: true, the main axis continues to grow
solution.why_others_wrong: Basipetal order belongs to cymose inflorescence, where growth of the main axis is limited.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Inflorescence
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about leaves are correct?

(a) China rose, mustard and sunflower show alternate phyllotaxy.
(b) Calotropis and guava show opposite phyllotaxy.
(c) Alstonia shows whorled phyllotaxy.
(d) Neem has palmately compound leaves.
(e) Silk cotton has palmately compound leaves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alternate: a single leaf at each node (china rose, mustard, sunflower). Opposite: a pair at each node (Calotropis, guava). Whorled: more than two at a node (Alstonia). Neem has pinnately compound leaves (leaflets on a common rachis); silk cotton has palmately compound leaves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf (types of leaves, phyllotaxy)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (type of placentation) with List-II (example).

List-I:
A. Marginal
B. Parietal
C. Free central
D. Basal

List-II:
I. Dianthus
II. Marigold
III. Pea
IV. Argemone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Marginal: placenta along the ventral suture of a one-chambered ovary (pea). Parietal: ovules on the inner wall or periphery (mustard, Argemone). Free central: ovules on a central axis without septa (Dianthus, Primrose). Basal: a single ovule at the base (sunflower, marigold).
solution.why_others_wrong: Dianthus (free central) and Argemone (parietal) are the pair most often swapped.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (gynoecium, placentation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In perigynous flowers such as plum, rose and peach, the ovary is said to be half inferior.
Statement II: In epigynous flowers such as guava and cucumber, the ovary is inferior.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Position of floral parts on the thalamus
solution.explanation: Hypogynous: ovary highest, superior (mustard, china rose, brinjal). Perigynous: other parts at about the level of the ovary, which is half inferior (plum, rose, peach). Epigynous: thalamus grows round the ovary and fuses with it, other parts above it, so the ovary is inferior (guava, cucumber, ray florets of sunflower).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (position of floral parts)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a maize grain, the proteinaceous layer that separates the endosperm from the embryo is the:

solution.explanation: In maize, the outer covering of the bulky endosperm separates it from the embryo by a proteinous layer called the aleurone layer. The embryo has one large shield-shaped cotyledon (scutellum) and an axis with the plumule and radicle enclosed in sheaths: coleoptile and coleorhiza.
steps: Aleurone layer: between endosperm and embryo
Coleoptile / coleorhiza: sheaths of plumule / radicle
solution.why_others_wrong: The scutellum is the cotyledon; the coleoptile and coleorhiza are sheaths of the plumule and radicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Seed (structure of a monocotyledonous seed)
solution.final_answer: Option B: aleurone layer

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The floral formula % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1 represents a flower of the family:

solution.explanation: % = zygomorphic; C1+2+(2) = papilionaceous corolla (one standard, two wings, two fused keel petals); A(9)+1 = diadelphous stamens; G1 = monocarpellary ovary. These are the features of Fabaceae (e.g. pea).
solution.why_others_wrong: Solanaceae is ⊕ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2); Liliaceae is ⊕ P(3+3) A3+3 G(3).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of some important families (Fabaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Fabaceae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the family Solanaceae are correct?

(a) The stamens are five and epipetalous.
(b) The ovary is bicarpellary, obliquely placed, syncarpous and superior, with axile placentation.
(c) The corolla has five free petals with imbricate aestivation.
(d) The seeds are non-endospermous.
(e) Belladonna and ashwagandha are medicinal plants of this family.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Solanaceae: actinomorphic flowers; calyx of five united sepals, persistent, valvate; corolla of five united petals, valvate; five epipetalous stamens; bicarpellary, obliquely placed, syncarpous, superior, bilocular ovary with axile placentation; berry or capsule; seeds many and endospermous. Belladonna and ashwagandha are medicinal members.
steps: (c) False: the corolla is united (gamopetalous), valvate
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of some important families (Solanaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (member of Fabaceae) with List-II (use).

List-I:
A. Indigofera
B. Sunhemp
C. Sesbania
D. Muliathi

List-II:
I. Medicine
II. Fodder
III. Dye
IV. Fibre

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT lists Fabaceae plants as sources of pulses, edible oil, dye (Indigofera), fibres (sunhemp), fodder (Sesbania, Trifolium), ornamentals (lupin, sweet pea) and medicine (muliathi).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of some important families (Fabaceae, economic importance)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The floral formula of Liliaceae shows P(3+3) in place of separate K and C.
Reason (R): In Liliaceae the calyx and corolla are not distinct, so they are together termed the perianth (tepals).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: When calyx and corolla are not distinct, they are called the perianth, as in lily. Liliaceae has six tepals in two whorls of three, often united into a tube, written P(3+3). R is exactly why the formula uses P.
steps: A: Br ⊕ ⚥ P(3+3) A3+3 G(3) → true
R: tepals = undifferentiated calyx and corolla → true
Undistinguished calyx and corolla are written as P → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (perianth); Description of some important families (Liliaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All monocotyledonous seeds are endospermic.
Statement II: In bean, gram and pea, the endosperm persists in the mature seed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Monocot seeds are generally endospermic, but some, as in orchids, are non-endospermic, so 'all' makes Statement I false. In bean, gram and pea the endosperm is not present in the mature seed (non-endospermous seeds), so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement I: false (orchid seeds are non-endospermic)
Statement II: false (bean, gram, pea are non-endospermous)
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I is a trap based on the word 'all': NCERT says 'generally', and names orchids as the exception.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Seed
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about flowers are correct?

(a) Stamens attached to the perianth, as in lily, are called epiphyllous.
(b) The stamens of china rose are united into one bundle (monoadelphous).
(c) In Cassia and gulmohur, the margins of the petals overlap one another, but not in any particular direction.
(d) Citrus has polyadelphous stamens.
(e) Brinjal has epiphyllous stamens.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Stamens attached to petals are epipetalous (brinjal); attached to the perianth, epiphyllous (lily). Stamens may be united in one bundle (monoadelphous, china rose), two bundles (diadelphous, pea) or more than two bundles (polyadelphous, citrus). Imbricate aestivation: margins overlap but not in a particular direction (Cassia, gulmohur).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (aestivation, androecium)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Grasses regenerate the parts removed by grazing herbivores mainly through the activity of:

solution.explanation: Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues. They are found in grasses and regenerate parts removed by grazing herbivores.
steps: Found in grasses → regrowth after grazing
solution.why_others_wrong: The root apical meristem adds to root length; cork cambium and vascular cambium are lateral meristems, not meristems lying between mature tissues.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (meristematic tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option C: intercalary meristems

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In grasses, the guard cells of the stomata are:

solution.explanation: Each stoma has two guard cells. Guard cells are generally bean-shaped; in grasses they are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls are thin and the inner walls (towards the pore) highly thickened.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bean-shaped guard cells are the general type, not the grass type. Guard cells are present in grasses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (epidermal tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option D: dumb-bell shaped

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The Casparian strips of the endodermis of a root are made of:

solution.explanation: The tangential and radial walls of root endodermal cells have water-impermeable, waxy suberin deposited as Casparian strips.
steps: Endodermis: innermost layer of the cortex
Casparian strips: suberin on radial and tangential walls
solution.why_others_wrong: Lignin thickens xylem walls, cutin forms the cuticle and pectin thickens collenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous plants (dicot root)
solution.final_answer: Option A: suberin

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Vessels are absent from the xylem of gymnosperms.
Statement II: Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells instead of companion cells and sieve tubes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Vessels are a characteristic feature of angiosperms; gymnosperms lack them. Gymnosperm phloem lacks sieve tubes and companion cells; it has sieve cells and albuminous cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (xylem, phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (tissue or cell) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Collenchyma
B. Sclereids
C. Companion cells
D. Phloem fibres

List-II:
I. Commercial fibres of jute, flax and hemp
II. Their nucleus controls the functions of sieve tubes
III. Walls thickened at the corners with cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin
IV. Found in the pulp of guava, pear and sapota

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Collenchyma has corner thickenings of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin. Sclereids occur in the fruit walls of nuts, the pulp of guava, pear and sapota, seed coats of legumes and tea leaves. The nucleus of the companion cell controls the sieve tube. Phloem (bast) fibres of jute, flax and hemp are used commercially.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sclereids and phloem fibres are both sclerenchyma, but only phloem fibres give commercial fibres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (permanent tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Grass leaves curl inwards when water is scarce.
Reason (R): Bulliform cells in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves become flaccid when they lose water.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Some adaxial epidermal cells along the veins of grass leaves are large, empty and colourless (bulliform cells). When turgid, they keep the leaf surface exposed; when flaccid under water stress, they make the leaf curl inwards to reduce water loss. R explains A.
steps: Flaccid bulliform cells cause the inward curling → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous plants (monocot leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about xylem are correct?

(a) In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre and the metaxylem towards the periphery.
(b) In roots, the protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem towards the centre.
(c) Vessels are a characteristic feature of angiosperms.
(d) Tracheids are living, thin-walled cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Endarch xylem (stems): protoxylem towards the centre. Exarch xylem (roots): protoxylem towards the periphery. Vessels are characteristic of angiosperms. Tracheids are dead, elongated cells with thick, lignified walls and tapering ends.
steps: (d) False: tracheids are dead with lignified walls
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A monocot root usually has more than six xylem bundles (polyarch).
Statement II: In a monocot root, the pith is small or inconspicuous.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A monocot root resembles a dicot root but usually has more than six xylem bundles (polyarch), while a dicot root has two to four. The pith of a monocot root is large and well developed; in a dicot root it is small or inconspicuous.
steps: Statement II: false, the pith is large and well developed
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II describes the dicot root.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous plants (monocot root)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about trichomes in the shoot system is correct?

options.text: They are elongations of root epidermal cells.
They help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

solution.explanation: Root hairs are unicellular elongations of root epidermal cells. Trichomes on the shoot are usually multicellular, branched or unbranched, soft or stiff, and may be secretory. They help prevent water loss due to transpiration.
steps: Shoot trichomes: usually multicellular, may be secretory
solution.why_others_wrong: Unicellular elongations of root epidermis are root hairs. Trichomes are usually multicellular and can be secretory.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (epidermal tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option D: They help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are features of a monocot stem?

(a) A sclerenchymatous hypodermis.
(b) Conjoint, closed vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.
(c) Absence of phloem parenchyma.
(d) Vascular bundles arranged in a ring.
(e) Water-containing cavities within the vascular bundles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis and many scattered vascular bundles, each with a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath. The bundles are conjoint and closed, the peripheral ones smaller. Phloem parenchyma is absent and water-containing cavities are present in the bundles. A ring of bundles is a dicot stem feature.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous plants (monocot stem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (anatomical feature) with List-II (organ).

List-I:
A. Endodermis rich in starch grains (starch sheath)
B. Mesophyll differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma
C. Two to four xylem patches
D. Undifferentiated mesophyll with stomata on both surfaces

List-II:
I. Dicot root
II. Isobilateral leaf
III. Dicot stem
IV. Dorsiventral leaf

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In a dicot stem, the endodermis is rich in starch grains and called the starch sheath. A dorsiventral (dicot) leaf has palisade and spongy mesophyll. A dicot root usually has two to four xylem and phloem patches. An isobilateral (monocot) leaf has stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll.
solution.why_others_wrong: The root endodermis has Casparian strips; the starch sheath is the endodermis of the dicot stem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous plants
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The vascular bundles of roots are of the radial type.
Reason (R): In roots, the xylem and phloem are arranged on the same radius.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In roots, xylem and phloem lie in an alternate manner on different radii; this arrangement is called radial. In conjoint bundles (stems, leaves) xylem and phloem lie together on the same radius. So A is true and R is false.
steps: R: false, the same-radius arrangement defines conjoint bundles
solution.why_others_wrong: R describes conjoint vascular bundles, the opposite of radial.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (vascular tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A mature sieve tube element retains a large nucleus that controls its functions.
Statement II: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocotyledons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A mature sieve element has peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus; its functions are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell. Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocots.
steps: Statement I: false, a mature sieve element lacks a nucleus
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Who explained that new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula)?

solution.explanation: Schleiden (1838) and Schwann (1839) together formulated the cell theory, but it did not explain how new cells form. Rudolf Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divide and new cells form from pre-existing cells, and he modified the hypothesis into the final form of the cell theory.
steps: Schleiden: all plants are made of cells
Schwann: animals; plasma membrane; cell wall unique to plants
solution.why_others_wrong: Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory without explaining the origin of new cells; Robert Brown discovered the nucleus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Theory
solution.final_answer: Option C: Rudolf Virchow

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the endomembrane system?

solution.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles work in coordination and form the endomembrane system. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not included because their functions are not coordinated with these components.
steps: Endomembrane system = ER + Golgi complex + lysosomes + vacuoles
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System
solution.final_answer: Option D: Peroxisome

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which cell organelle is the inner membrane folded into infoldings called cristae?

solution.explanation: A mitochondrion has two membranes. The inner membrane forms infoldings called cristae towards the matrix, which increase its surface area.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chloroplasts have flattened thylakoids stacked as grana, not cristae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Mitochondria
solution.final_answer: Option B: Mitochondrion

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The material of the nucleus that stains with basic dyes was named chromatin by:

solution.explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus as a cell organelle (1831). Later, the nuclear material stained by basic dyes was named chromatin by Flemming.
solution.why_others_wrong: Golgi discovered the Golgi apparatus; Palade observed ribosomes as dense particles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus
solution.final_answer: Option C: Flemming

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The axoneme of cilia and flagella has a 9 + 2 arrangement of microtubules.
Statement II: Each of the nine peripheral fibrils of a centriole is a doublet of microtubules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The axoneme has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules and a pair of central microtubules (9 + 2). A centriole has a cartwheel organisation of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin, each a triplet.
steps: Statement II: false, centriole fibrils are triplets
solution.why_others_wrong: Doublets belong to the axoneme; centriole fibrils are triplets.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cilia and Flagella; Centrosome and Centrioles
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure in a prokaryotic cell) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Mesosome
B. Plasmid
C. Fimbriae
D. Chromatophores

List-II:
I. Membranous extensions containing pigments, as in cyanobacteria
II. Small circular DNA that can confer antibiotic resistance
III. Infolding of the plasma membrane that helps in cell wall formation and DNA replication
IV. Small bristle-like fibres that help the cell attach to rocks in streams and to host tissues

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane (vesicles, tubules, lamellae) that help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution, respiration and secretion. Plasmids are small circular extra-chromosomal DNA that can give antibiotic resistance. Fimbriae help attachment. Chromatophores are pigment-containing membranous extensions in cyanobacteria.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mesosomes and chromatophores are both membranous extensions, but only chromatophores carry pigments.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Proteins can move laterally within the plasma membrane.
Reason (R): The lipid bilayer of the plasma membrane is quasi-fluid in nature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model (Singer and Nicolson), the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer lets proteins move laterally within it. This fluidity is important for cell growth, intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis and cell division. R is the reason for A.
steps: A: lateral movement of proteins → true
Fluid lipid layer allows the movement → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Membrane
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The middle lamella, which holds neighbouring plant cells together, is mainly made of calcium pectate.
Statement II: The secondary wall of a plant cell is formed on the outer side of the primary wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate that glues neighbouring cells together. The primary wall of a young cell can grow; it diminishes as the cell matures, and the secondary wall is formed on the inner side of the cell (towards the membrane).
steps: Statement II: false, the secondary wall forms on the inner side
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Wall
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the Golgi apparatus and lysosomes are correct?

(a) The cis face of the Golgi apparatus is the forming face and the trans face is the maturing face.
(b) The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
(c) Lysosomal enzymes are optimally active at alkaline pH.
(d) Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
(e) The Golgi apparatus was first observed by Robert Brown.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed the Golgi apparatus. Its cis (forming) and trans (maturing) faces are interconnected. It packages materials and is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. Lysosomes are vesicles formed by packaging in the Golgi; their hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) are optimally active at acidic pH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System (Golgi apparatus, lysosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the term '80S ribosome', the sedimentation coefficient indirectly indicates the ribosome's:

solution.explanation: 'S' (Svedberg unit) stands for the sedimentation coefficient. It is an indirect measure of density and size. Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S (60S + 40S); prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S (50S + 30S).
steps: It indirectly measures density and size
solution.why_others_wrong: S values are not counts of molecules, and they do not measure activity. That is also why 60S + 40S gives 80S, not 100S.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Ribosomes
solution.final_answer: Option C: density and size

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Larger and more numerous nucleoli are present in cells that are actively carrying out protein synthesis.
Reason (R): The nucleolus is not a membrane-bound structure; its content is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis, so cells making a lot of protein have larger and more numerous nucleoli. It is not membrane-bound, so its content is continuous with the nucleoplasm. Both statements are true, but the lack of a membrane does not explain A; rRNA synthesis does.
steps: The explanation of A is rRNA synthesis for ribosomes, not the absence of a membrane → R does not explain A
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap; R is a true but unrelated structural fact.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus (nucleolus)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about plastids are correct?

(a) Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls.
(b) Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), as in potato.
(c) Aleuroplasts store oils and fats.
(d) The stroma of a chloroplast contains small, double-stranded circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Chromoplasts give yellow, orange or red colours (carotenoids). Leucoplasts are colourless storage plastids: amyloplasts store starch (potato), elaioplasts store oils and fats, aleuroplasts store proteins. The chloroplast stroma has small circular dsDNA and 70S ribosomes.
steps: (c) False: aleuroplasts store proteins; elaioplasts store oils and fats
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (type of chromosome) with List-II (position of the centromere).

List-I:
A. Metacentric
B. Sub-metacentric
C. Acrocentric
D. Telocentric

List-II:
I. At the tip (terminal)
II. Close to one end, giving one extremely short and one very long arm
III. In the middle, giving two equal arms
IV. Slightly away from the middle, giving one shorter and one longer arm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Classification of chromosomes by centromere position
solution.explanation: Metacentric: centromere in the middle, two equal arms. Sub-metacentric: slightly away from the middle, one shorter and one longer arm. Acrocentric: close to the end, one extremely short and one very long arm. Telocentric: terminal centromere.
solution.why_others_wrong: Acrocentric (near the end) and telocentric (at the end) are the pair most often confused.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus (chromosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about cilia, flagella and centrioles are correct?

(a) The central microtubules of the axoneme are connected by bridges and enclosed by a central sheath.
(b) The central sheath is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublet by a radial spoke.
(c) Cilia and flagella emerge from centriole-like structures called basal bodies.
(d) The two centrioles of a centrosome lie parallel to each other.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In the axoneme the two central microtubules are joined by bridges and enclosed by a central sheath, which is linked to one tubule of each peripheral doublet by radial spokes. Cilia and flagella arise from basal bodies. The centrosome has two cylindrical centrioles lying perpendicular to each other.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cilia and Flagella; Centrosome and Centrioles
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lipids make up about 52 per cent of the membrane of human erythrocytes.
Reason (R): The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Biochemical study of the human RBC membrane shows about 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids. So A, which gives 52 per cent to lipids, is false. R is true: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.
steps: RBC membrane: ~52% protein, ~40% lipid → A false
Fluid mosaic model: Singer and Nicolson, 1972 → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: The trap is the swapped percentages; protein, not lipid, is about 52 per cent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Membrane
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In plant cells, vacuoles can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
(b) Because the tonoplast transports ions against concentration gradients, their concentration is much higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
(c) In Amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion.
(d) The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site of protein synthesis.
(e) In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The plant vacuole can fill up to 90 per cent of the cell; the tonoplast pumps ions into it against the gradient. The contractile vacuole of Amoeba helps in osmoregulation and excretion. Rough ER, with ribosomes, is active in protein synthesis and secretion; smooth ER is the major site of lipid synthesis, including steroidal hormones in animal cells.
steps: (d) False: RER makes proteins; SER makes lipids
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System (ER, vacuoles)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Prokaryotic ribosomes are of the 80S type, made of 60S and 40S subunits.
Statement II: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells is stored in inclusion bodies bounded by a single membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Ribosomes and inclusion bodies of prokaryotes
solution.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits; 80S (60S + 40S) ribosomes are eukaryotic. Inclusion bodies (phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, glycogen granules) are not bounded by any membrane and lie free in the cytoplasm.
steps: Statement II: false, inclusion bodies have no membrane
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (ribosomes and inclusion bodies)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which change takes place during the S phase of the cell cycle?

options.text: The number of chromosomes doubles, but the amount of DNA stays the same.
The amount of DNA doubles, but the number of chromosomes stays the same.
Both the amount of DNA and the number of chromosomes double.
Both the amount of DNA and the number of chromosomes are halved.

solution.explanation: DNA replicates during the S phase. If the initial amount of DNA is 2C, it becomes 4C. Each chromosome now has two chromatids joined at the centromere, so the chromosome number is unchanged (a 2n cell stays 2n).
steps: Chromosome number: 2n → 2n (each chromosome now has two chromatids)
solution.why_others_wrong: Chromosome number doubles only briefly at anaphase, when sister chromatids separate; it is halved by meiosis I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (phases of cell cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option B: The amount of DNA doubles, but the number of chromosomes stays the same.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied at which stage of mitosis?

solution.explanation: By metaphase, condensation of chromosomes is complete and they line up at the metaphase plate. They can be observed clearly under the microscope, so this is the stage at which their morphology is most easily studied.
steps: Chromosomes aligned at the metaphase plate
solution.why_others_wrong: In prophase condensation is incomplete, in anaphase the chromatids are moving apart, and in telophase the chromosomes decondense.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (metaphase)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Metaphase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A single cell divides repeatedly by mitosis, and in every round each cell divides once. How many rounds of division are needed to produce 128 cells?

solution.concept: Mitosis doubles the number of cells
solution.explanation: Each mitotic division gives two daughter cells, so the cell number doubles in every round: after n rounds there are 2ⁿ cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 rounds give only 64 cells; 64 is half the number of cells, not the number of rounds. 127 is the total number of individual division events (1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 64), not the number of rounds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase; Significance of Mitosis
solution.final_answer: Option B: 7

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Mitosis results in diploid daughter cells with an identical genetic complement.
Statement II: Meiosis increases the genetic variability in the population of organisms from one generation to the next.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Mitosis is an equational division: daughter cells have the same chromosome number and genetic complement as the parent. Meiosis conserves the chromosome number across sexually reproducing generations and increases genetic variability, which is important for evolution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis; Significance of Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of prophase I) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Leptotene
B. Zygotene
C. Pachytene
D. Diplotene

List-II:
I. Crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes
II. Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex; chiasmata become visible
III. Chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope
IV. Synapsis of homologous chromosomes with formation of the synaptonemal complex

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Leptotene: chromosomes become visible as compaction continues. Zygotene: homologues pair (synapsis) with a synaptonemal complex, forming bivalents. Pachytene: crossing over. Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and the homologues separate except at chiasmata.
solution.why_others_wrong: Crossing over happens in pachytene; chiasmata, its visible sign, appear in diplotene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A diploid cell in G1 phase contains 20 pg of DNA. It enters meiosis. How much DNA will each cell have at the end of meiosis I (before meiosis II begins)? There is no DNA replication during interkinesis.

solution.explanation: DNA doubles in the S phase before meiosis. Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes into two cells, halving the DNA. Interkinesis has no DNA replication, and meiosis II halves it again.
steps: After meiosis I: each cell 2C = 20 pg
solution.shortcut: Meiosis I starts at 4C and ends at 2C: the G1 value again.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 pg is the content after meiosis II; 40 pg is the content after S phase (G2); 5 pg halves too many times.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (S phase); Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option C: 20 pg

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells in the quiescent stage (G0) are metabolically inactive.
Reason (R): Cells in G0 do not proliferate unless called on to do so, depending on the requirement of the organism.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Some cells, such as heart cells in adult animals, do not divide further; others divide only occasionally. Cells that do not divide further exit G1 and enter G0. NCERT states that cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so.
steps: A: false, G0 cells are metabolically active
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Inactive' is the trap: G0 cells are non-dividing, not non-metabolising.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (phases of cell cycle, G0)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In animal cells, cytokinesis takes place by the formation of a cell plate that grows from the centre outwards.
Statement II: The liquid endosperm of coconut is a multinucleate condition that arises when karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In animal cells a furrow appears in the plasma membrane and deepens until the cytoplasm divides in two. Plant cells, enclosed by a rigid wall, form a cell plate from the centre outwards. When karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, a multinucleate syncytium forms, e.g. the liquid endosperm of coconut.
steps: Statement I: false, cell plate formation is in plant cells
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about mitosis are correct?

(a) At the end of prophase, the Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and nuclear envelope are no longer seen.
(b) Kinetochores are small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromere that serve as attachment sites for spindle fibres.
(c) In anaphase, the arms of each chromosome lead the way to the pole and the centromere trails behind.
(d) In telophase, chromosomes cluster at opposite poles and their identity as discrete elements is lost.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Late prophase: Golgi, ER, nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear. Metaphase: spindle fibres attach to kinetochores. Anaphase: centromeres split, and the chromatids move to the poles with the centromere leading and the arms trailing. Telophase: chromosomes decondense at the poles and lose their individuality; the nuclear envelope and nucleolus reappear.
steps: (c) False: the centromere leads, the arms trail
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant cell with 2n = 16 divides by mitosis. How many chromatids are present in the cell at metaphase, and how many chromosomes are present in the whole cell at anaphase?

solution.concept: Chromatid and chromosome counts during mitosis
solution.explanation: After the S phase each of the 16 chromosomes has two sister chromatids, giving 32 chromatids at metaphase. At anaphase the centromeres split and each chromatid becomes a daughter chromosome, so the cell briefly holds 32 chromosomes (16 moving to each pole).
steps: Anaphase: centromeres split → 32 chromosomes (16 at each pole)
solution.why_others_wrong: 16 chromatids forgets that DNA replicated in S phase. 16 chromosomes at anaphase counts only one pole or forgets that separated chromatids are counted as chromosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (metaphase, anaphase)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 32 chromatids and 32 chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about meiosis are correct?

(a) Crossing over is an enzyme-mediated process, and the enzyme involved is recombinase.
(b) In the oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
(c) DNA replicates during interkinesis.
(d) Sister chromatids separate from each other during anaphase I.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Crossing over in pachytene is mediated by the enzyme recombinase. Diplotene can last for months or years in oocytes of some vertebrates. Interkinesis is generally short-lived and has no DNA replication. In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay associated at their centromeres; sister chromatids separate in anaphase II.
steps: (c) False: no DNA replication in interkinesis
(d) False: homologues separate in anaphase I
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) describes anaphase II (or mitotic anaphase), the commonest meiosis trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis.
Reason (R): Meiosis II begins immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes have fully elongated.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In meiosis II the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate, just as in mitosis, which is why it resembles mitosis. NCERT also states that meiosis II starts immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes fully elongate. That is true, but its timing does not explain the similarity to mitosis.
steps: The resemblance comes from separation of sister chromatids, not the timing of onset → R does not explain A
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap: R describes when meiosis II begins, not why it is mitosis-like.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In animals, mitotic cell division is seen only in diploid somatic cells.
Statement II: In plants, mitotic divisions occur only in diploid cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in animals, mitotic division is seen only in diploid somatic cells. Against this, plants can show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells (for example, the haploid gametophytes).
steps: Statement II: false, plants show mitosis in haploid and diploid cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Treating plants like animals is the trap; haploid plant cells also divide by mitosis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (introduction to mitosis)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When the pigments of a green leaf are separated by paper chromatography, chlorophyll b appears:
